hostMonitor.scope: Shared host. No owned builds, test suites or profiling ran during measured windows. Window wall-clock boundaries are approximate, derived from the first deadline progress observation.

httpResponseInterpretation: Classify HTTP409 conversation consistency conflicts separately from HTTP503 availability failures. The baseline messages/turns handlers return recoverable409 responses for changed revisions or stale cursors. This capture retains paths and statuses, not response bodies, so the precise409 branch is not established.
limitations: Plugin capture counts requests and response statuses, not transferred bytes. Core WebSocket history requests remain a separate metric.
The complete E2E plugin also adds navigation, toolbar and review contributions. This is not a standalone conversation-only plugin or evidence about arbitrary plugins.
Stored history differs from the loaded newest window. Setup and plugin installation are outside timing and are not cold-entry metrics.
No M2 Air, field INP, battery or leak claim follows.

availability.interpretation: Baseline409 conversation conflicts are distinct from503 availability failures. Baselinepairs3,4,5 contain503 responses; the backend records table_probe deadline failures. All content eventually passed, but these failures and verification retries remain in the result. The candidate already includes the reader-pool health repair. No general availability rate is inferred.

conclusions: Streaming core history requests fall 95.58% and decoded history bytes fall 95.57% by median paired change. Both improve in all six pairs; full-history resets fall to zero.
Plugin conversation HTTP requests during streaming fall from 364–596 per baseline sample to zero in every candidate sample. Setup traffic and scheduled core backfill remain separate.
Streaming renderer CPU falls 12.62% and main-thread CPU falls 8.29% by median paired change. Each improves in five pairs and regresses in pair 4.
Streaming frame-gap p95 improves in five pairs and is effectively equal in one. Its median paired reduction is 49.70%. Maximum gap regresses in pair 3, from 116.7 to 150 ms.
Streaming main-thread task time falls 5.94%, below the 20% target. Normal-idle CPU is mixed, including material regressions.

Reduced-motion idle main-thread CPU falls 12.35% by median paired change, with two regressing pairs. Four animations remain running in every candidate reduced-motion sample, compared with 49 in baseline. The core-only candidate had zero. The four targets and their CPU contribution are not yet identified.
Nine API panels and four document editors remain present in every sample. Every hidden chat catches up to 300 ordered ticks and preserves its draft.
Shared-host load ranges from 0.45 to 14.89 and available memory falls to 15,076,704 KiB. Correlation alone does not attribute the regressions.

findings: Normal-idle main CPU increases 21.21% in pair 3 and 27.22% in pair 5. Main-thread task time increases 21.14% and 43.96% in those pairs.
Streaming main CPU increases 6.05%, renderer CPU 1.57%, and main-thread task time 8.44% in pair 4.

Reduced-motion main CPU increases 7.75% and 7.14% in the first two pairs. Maximum frame gaps regress in the first five reduced-motion pairs, including 33.4 to 483.308 ms in pair 2. Do not infer uniform smoothness from p95.

Candidate running animations are 51 in normal motion and four in reduced motion. The core-only candidate had 47 and zero. The full plugin also adds a hidden review pane, so the extra animation source must be observed before attribution.
regressionInvestigation.nextStep: Use a separate opt-in CPU/animation capture for each window. Do not pool profiles with timing or alter the fixed plugin fixture to manufacture a gain.
